newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan activists to fish near disupted islands.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan activists to fish near disupted islands.

text.p: Taiwan activists said on Sunday they would join colleagues from New York and Hong Kong for a fishing competition near disputed islands in the East China Sea on May 22.
They plan to leave a Taiwan port on Thursday evening and hold a fishing competition around 12 nautical miles off the islands, the activists said in a statement.
They said they were just following a government policy which encourages healthy outdoor sports, but the trip is seen as part of moves to take back the islands from the Japanese.

Hong Kong activists said on Saturday they had bought a 21-metre (69 ft) vessel for HK$500,000 (US$65,000) to sail to the rocky outcrops between Taiwan and Japan's Okinawa island chain next week to reclaim them from the Japanese.
They said it would take three days for the dozen activists to arrive at the islands, known as Diaoyu in China and Senkakus in Japan. China, Japan and Taiwan all claim ownership of them.
Taiwan and Hong Kong activists last week called off a planned trip to the islands from Taiwan because of a shortage of funds and pressure from the Taiwanese government.

The construction of a lighthouse on one of the islands by a Japanese rightist group in 1996 lit nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan and sparked a wave of landing attempts, during which a Hong Kong activist drowned.
Activists have staged fresh protest marches and demonstrations outside Japan's consulate after several Japanese nationalists landed recently on the islands.

In October 1996, Taiwan and Hong Kong activists broke through a Japanese maritime cordon, went ashore on one of the islands and hoisted the flags of China and Taiwan in a bid to assert Chinese sovereignty over the rocky outcrops.
